pr_title: Allow combining of position and state of MQTT cover

## Breaking change
This might make some mqtt covers report badly, if they are badly implemented.
If they support state and position, but state until now was bad and ignored, now it would not. 
**BUT I would like someone else to validate this this is actually breaking, ...**

You now have to choose between state or position. I want to know the position and know if the cover is moving
For this the position code should not update the state, and let this be done by state messages.

Hey there @home-assistant/core, @emontnemery, mind taking a look at this pull request as its been labeled with an integration (`mqtt`) you are listed as a [codeowner](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/CODEOWNERS#L284) for? Thanks!
<sub><sup>(message by CodeOwnersMention)</sup></sub>

Hi @frenck, 

I like the idea that you can use the position topic and the status topic together. 
But some devices as e.G. Shelly does publish "opening", "closing" and "stop", but no "closed" and "opened". 
So it would be good if the actual position logic for states is not ignored completly if a state topic is configured.

I thing you should look after the state_closed and state_opened as well. 
If they where configured manually e.g. `none` (overwriting the default value) than the logic of the position should still take place (to my knowledge: 0 means closed, >0 means open), but the opening/closing states should be taken from the mqtt state topic.

That would allow shelly devices to take advantage of the new feature as well. A shelly publishes a new position only after it has reached the new position, so during that time "opening" would be the actual status.

Sebastian

issue_context.title: MQTT Cover sets state based on position, even if state topic is configured.
issue_context.body:
https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/a47cf27ed6a9028e1d1af8e186452b0140fee8bd/homeassistant/components/mqtt/cover.py#L336

Because state is always set when a position is received, we lose state information like 'closing' and 'opening'
State should only be set by position if:
- State topic is not set
- Optionally when position is 0 or 100, but even then, ...

Hey there @home-assistant/core, @emontnemery, mind taking a look at this issue as its been labeled with an integration (`mqtt`) you are listed as a [codeowner](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/CODEOWNERS#L284) for? Thanks!
<sub><sup>(message by CodeOwnersMention)</sup></sub>

Oh, yes, this would be great!
Right now the Tasmota integration (that uses MQTT as well as far as my knowledge goes) has that already in it. 
Tasmota uses position = 0  -> closed, position <> 0 -> open from the position topic and opening/closing from the stat topic.
It would be great, if the MQTT-integration would have the same behavior...
There might be a chance, as emontnemery had his hands on both integrations :-)

Seb

review_comments: @CubieMedia can you explain the logic for this `or self._position is None`, we only reach here if we have a numeric payload.

This solves a problem that exists on restarting Home Assistant. The device sends the stop state (cover is not moving) but we can not determine the real state (closed, open), for this we need the position. So what the change does, it takes the first position message (self._position is None) to also set the state.

> we only reach here if we have a numeric payload.

This is correct and should stay that way, the code only differs if self._position has been set before. That is why we have to set position afterwards. Otherwise we would not know if it has been set.
